summary.verdict: The implementation conforms to the motor_022 contract. It evaluates supplied phase contracts, version records, quality records and harness results without modifying upstream objects; emits ConformanceRecord, ViolationRecord and DriftSignal structures; preserves versioning, lineage and evidence references; rejects malformed inputs with structured errors; and prevents PASS when material contract, boundary, lineage, quality or harness violations are present.

findings: EvaluationConformanceEngine.run exposes the documented core inputs: phase_contracts, version_records, quality_records and harness_results, with explicit optional target selection and read-only evaluated artifact context.
The output payload uses the documented keys conformance_record, violation_log and architectural_drift_signal, backed by frozen dataclass models for ConformanceRecord, ViolationRecord and DriftSignal.

Input validation enforces collection shape, required contract fields, version evidence, lineage compatibility, quality status values, harness target versions and evidence references before evaluation proceeds.

Structured rejection paths cover documented malformed conditions including ERROR_INVALID_INPUT_COLLECTION, ERROR_MISSING_TARGET_VERSION, ERROR_INVALID_STATUS, ERROR_MISSING_VERSION_RECORD and ERROR_MISSING_CONTRACT.
Conformance status is derived from linked violations: material violations force FAIL, non-material evidence gaps or warnings produce WARNING, and PASS is allowed only with no violations.
The implementation checks output invariants so a PASS record cannot carry violations, a FAIL record requires a material ViolationRecord and DriftSignal records require linked violation evidence.

ConformanceRecord includes the schema-required identifiers, evaluated object fields, contract references, lineage_id, quality_record_ids, harness_result_ids, status fields, violation_ids, drift_signal_ids and evidence_refs.
ViolationRecord entries include conformance_record_id, evaluated object/version, violation_type, rule_ref, severity, input_ref, expected_condition, observed_value, material flag and evidence_refs.

DriftSignal entries include scope, basis, severity, related_violation_ids, related_conformance_record_ids and evidence_refs, and are emitted only from repeated material violations or critical single violations.
All emitted entities carry version_id, created_at, updated_at, version_hash, source_ref, produced_by_motor, produced_at and parent_id fields consistent with the technical schema.
Identifiers and version hashes are generated deterministically from canonicalized semantic payloads, while timestamps are passed as explicit evaluation context.
The engine deep-copies input bundles at entry and compares them before return, rejecting any detected upstream mutation during conformance evaluation.

test_results.coverage_assessment: Executable smoke verification covered the documented happy path and malformed phase_contracts rejection path. Artifact review also checked declared coverage for sparse evidence, invalid statuses, missing target versions, missing version records, missing contracts, material harness failures, boundary breaches, missing lineage and repeated-violation drift signals.
test_results.notes: The happy-path smoke run emitted ConformanceRecord.status PASS, an empty violation_log and no architectural_drift_signal. A malformed phase_contracts input was rejected through safe_run with ERROR_INVALID_INPUT_COLLECTION. No standalone pytest suite is packaged in this artifact, but the reviewed implementation and documented test specification cover the motor's required deterministic conformance behavior without upstream mutation.
